provenance.notes: Helix counts POINTS in a token bucket refilled every minute, one bucket for app access requests and one per user for user access requests; a request costs 1 point unless its endpoint says otherwise. The bucket's size is not stated as policy (800 appears in the guide's example header): not declared. The unit is points ("unit": "points"): a site that knows its bucket declares it, as Ratelimit-Limit says, e.g. {"max": 800, "window": "minute", "unit": "points", "cost": {"schedule": 2}} (schedule makes two requests, users and schedule; live one). Twitch's Ratelimit-Limit, Ratelimit-Remaining and Ratelimit-Reset headers are not the IETF fields; they are read as legacy fields, Ratelimit-Reset being "a Unix epoch timestamp" (the guide): no point left holds every call until the reset. A 429 is honoured. Developer Agreement (2024-12-04): Twitch content cached 24 hours at most and not shared, deleted items removed; re-syndicating or redistributing API data is prohibited, and Twitch data may not be sold, licensed or monetized absent a separate agreement; ads beside embeds only with other content of substantial value; a clear path to the source from every display, Twitch marks used only to attribute (twitch.tv/p/legal/trademark). Every request carries the Client-Id and an access token.
